P draws 0..7 and equals W in about half the cases (alias): P = W is the only position outside 0x512cc1's backward cycle L..W-1, the one case where 0x512cc1(6)/(0x14) return a real row instead of hitting the marker S (needed for the [0x88f628]/[0x88f62c] equality blocks at 0x512e11/0x512e19). U draws -1..7 (0x520584 stores -1). Row bounds: with W > L 0x512cc1 never returns below 0 (a wrap adds W-L >= 1), with W = L it returns at worst P-3 >= -3, and -1 on failure; when byte [0x7c2e82] is set that result becomes the start row (0x512dae), so the walk visits rows -3..7 (R+1 > W resets to L; P <= 7). The slot area [0x7a8e18] (row r at base + r*pitch, 'imul [0x6975c4]; add esi,[0x7a8e18]') is therefore a 0x23c00-byte buffer with base = buffer + 0x9c00 (3 rows of the largest pitch before it, 8 rows after: rows -3..7 plus a full-row rep movsb). Pitch [0x6975c4] is drawn from the real slot sizes 0x2d78/0x3400 (slot_00520b1b: state block + 0x2978) and the small 0x24/0x40 (the code is generic in it; all multiples of 4 so every row tag is a dword of the fill). The fill draws dwords mostly from {1,2,3} (the row tags 'cmp eax,1/2/3'; other values copy nothing), which also feeds the step [0x88f604] (row S + 0x20, read by 0x512d1a) and the +0x20 dword 0x512d3f rewrites in a full-row copy. N [0x7a8e1c] is the 'dec ecx; jne' walk count (0 would be 2^32 rows) and 0x512cc1's step limit: 1..24 with 20+ often (0x512cc1(0x14) needs N >= 20). Byte [0x7c2e82] ('test 0xff') and byte [0x88f5fc] (the 'cmp byte [0x88f5fc],0' after a -1 result) take both values. [0x88f5f8] is the save-buffer cursor 0x512f2a stores from edi after copying the state block: 0x512d68 rewrites dword [ptr + 0x6c + 0x20] through 0x512d3f, so it points at a 0x100-byte buffer. The wrap span [0x7a8e2c]-[0x7a8e28] of 0x512d3f is plain arithmetic (random). Every read stays inside the buffers for every draw, so nothing can fault.
